chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about singing/music, and I said: 'They claim that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the saying:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are lying!'

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. If We had wanted to take a pastime, We would have taken it from before Ourselves, if We were to do [so]. But We cast the truth against falsehood, so it demolishes it, and thereupon it vanishes. And for you is destruction from what you describe.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to so-and-so from what he described,' [referring to] a man who was not present in the gathering.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on singing and music in Shia hadith based on the refutation of the Prophet's permission?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the claim that the Prophet permitted specific singing lyrics, citing Quranic verses to show that creation was not for play or pastime. He emphasizes that casting truth against falsehood causes it to vanish, and concludes with a statement of 'woe' for those who describe or engage in such practices, even if they were not present at the specific gathering being discussed. This narration is central to the Shia jurisprudential debate on *al-ghina* (melodic singing), distinguishing between mere recitation and music that leads to heedlessness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdul A’ala who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the singing (music) and I said, ‘They (people) are claiming that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> allowed the saying (singing) of, ‘We have come to you, we have come to you! Greet us, greet us, we will greet you’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said:’

Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [21:16] And We did not Create the sky and the earth and what is between the two for sport [21:17] Had We Wanted to Take to a pass-time, We would have Taken it from before Ourselves had We wanted to Do (it) [21:18] But, We Cast the Truth against the falsehood, so that it breaks its head, and behold! It vanishes; and woe unto you for what you are describing’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto so and so from what he described a man who was not present in the gathering’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub from ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about music (and singing). I said that they think the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has granted permission in saying, ‘We have come to you, we have come to you, so offer us greetings, offer us greetings, we will offer you greetings.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘They have spoken a lie.

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “We did not create the heavens and the earth just for fun. [21:16] Had We wanted to play games, We could have certainly done so with things at hand. [21:17] We bring forward the Truth to crush and destroy falsehood; it is doomed to be banished. Woe to you for your way of thinking about Allah!” [21:18]’
He (the Imam) then said, ’Woe upon the one who ascribes something to one who is not present in the gathering.’”
